comparison: Perfect agreement on C1-C5. Both evaluations support the experimental design and dataset generation, with peer reviewers explicitly praising this as a 'tour de force' high-throughput imaging effort.
Perfect agreement on C6-C9. Both evaluations support the observations about genetic variation across RIAILs and the finding that phenotypically similar founders have different genetic bases.
Perfect agreement on C10-C12. Both evaluations support the statistical analysis rejecting the Timer model. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted this by not challenging it.

Partial disagreement on C13-C17. OpenEval finds the partial correlation analysis sound and well-supported, while peer reviewers marked it UNCERTAIN, requesting clarification on 'the link between partial correlations and correlations' as it 'does not seem to be obvious.'

Agreement on C18-C21. Both evaluations support the correlation analyses and rejection of the Boundary model, though peer reviewers later raised concerns about how the model accounts for other published findings.

Significant disagreement on C22-C29. OpenEval finds the QTL mapping approach appropriate and well-supported, while peer reviewers marked it UNCERTAIN, questioning novelty since 'gpr-1/2 and par-2 are important regulators...has been demonstrated many years ago.'

Disagreement on C30-C37, C40. OpenEval supports the linkage of QTLs to candidate genes through multiple lines of evidence, while peer reviewers marked it UNCERTAIN, noting this is 'not novel' and questioning whether model predictions match RNAi results.
OpenEval supports C41 (synthesis proposing force-balance mechanism based on gpr-1 and par-2 identification). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific synthesis claim.

Major disagreement on C42-C44. OpenEval finds the cup-cut ablation experiments provide strong evidence for net pulling forces, while peer reviewers marked it UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about 'intrinsic caveats (incomplete ablation...side-effects...rapid repolymerization)' and noting missing controls and discrepancies with Garzon-Coral et al., 2016.

Disagreement on C45-C47. OpenEval supports the plane-cut ablation interpretation, while peer reviewers marked it UNCERTAIN, questioning the laser ablation methodology and noting contradictions with published work (Garzon-Coral et al., 2016).

Disagreement on C48-C51. OpenEval finds the spd-1(RNAi) results provide converging evidence against spindle elasticity, while peer reviewers marked it UNCERTAIN, finding it 'not really convincing' due to centrosome overshoot and questioning whether this matches model predictions.

Partial disagreement on C52-C55. OpenEval supports the perpendicular ablation experiments as key evidence for multidirectional pulling forces, while peer reviewers marked it UNCERTAIN, raising general concerns about all laser ablation experiments and requesting experiments on the anterior side as well.

Significant disagreement on C56-C65, C91-C93. OpenEval finds the mathematical model clearly defined with well-supported predictions, while peer reviewers marked it UNCERTAIN, stating 'The authors did not do a good job in explaining the mechanism' and requesting better explanation of how stoichiometry leads to centering.

Disagreement on C66-C70. OpenEval supports the computational testing ruling out CFG limitation, while peer reviewers marked it UNCERTAIN, questioning the overall model design for not accounting for LET-99's role in restricting cortical pulling forces.

Disagreement on C71-C76. OpenEval finds strong agreement between model prediction and experimental validation, while peer reviewers marked it UNCERTAIN, noting discrepancy with Krueger et al., 2010 where 'a single centrosome...moved to the cell center' in disagreement with results presented.

Partial disagreement on C77-C80. OpenEval supports the model's ability to explain asymmetric division, while peer reviewers marked it UNCERTAIN, questioning whether the model fully accounts for LET-99 and whether it represents a significant advance over Bouvrais et al., 2018.

Agreement on C81-C88. Both evaluations support the model's quantitative predictive power across evolutionary timescales. Peer reviewers acknowledged this as a strength, stating it 'explains the dynamics and variability of spindle scaling across different nematodes.'

Strong disagreement on C90, C94. OpenEval supports the conclusion that pulling forces alone are sufficient, while peer reviewers marked it UNSUPPORTED, noting 'clear discrepancy' with Garzon-Coral et al., 2016 which found pushing forces during anaphase, and questioning laser ablation methodology.

Partial disagreement on C95, C96, C103. OpenEval supports these conclusions about asymmetry and evolution as major conceptual advances, while peer reviewers marked them UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the cross-species data as impressive but questioning whether it represents significant advance over previous models and adequately accounts for known genetic regulators.
OpenEval supports C97-C102 as established background knowledge with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
